g: Estar + adjective in the imperfect
‘Ustedes estaban muertos’ uses imperfect estaban to describe an ongoing former condition, with muertos agreeing in number with ustedes.
e: En otro tiempo
This temporal expression means ‘formerly’ or ‘at one time’ and sets the past condition here against a later change.

g: Two imperfect descriptions
‘Andaban’ and ‘se conducían’ present habitual conduct in the past. Conducirse means ‘to behave’ and carries the pronoun se.
e: los que viven en la desobediencia
Los que means ‘those who.’ The phrase describes people characterized by disobedience; Spanish uses vivir en to express an abiding sphere.

g: Past participles as circumstantial modifiers
‘Impulsados ... siguiendo ...’ adds the forces and conduct accompanying vivíamos; impulsados agrees with the plural subject nosotros.
e: por naturaleza objeto de la ira de Dios
Por naturaleza means ‘by nature,’ while objeto de marks the target of something: here, ‘objects of God's wrath.’

g: Inserted relative clause
‘Dios, que es rico en misericordia,’ places a descriptive que-clause between the subject Dios and the continuation of the sentence.
e: por su gran amor por nosotros
The first por gives the motivating cause, ‘because of his great love’; the second belongs to amor por, ‘love for us.’

v: made us alive; gave us life
g: Aun cuando + imperfect indicative
‘Aun cuando estábamos muertos’ states an actual circumstance, so it uses indicative estábamos: ‘even when we were dead.’
e: Por gracia ustedes han sido salvados
Por marks the basis or means, not an agent. Han sido salvados is a present-perfect passive whose result remains relevant.

g: Hacer + infinitive
In ‘nos hizo sentar,’ preterite hizo plus infinitive sentar forms a causative construction: ‘he seated us.’ Nos is its object.
e: en unión con Cristo Jesús
En unión con means ‘in union with.’ It frames both coordinated past actions, resucitó and hizo sentar.

g: Para + infinitive of purpose
‘Para mostrar’ states the purpose of the preceding actions: ‘in order to show.’ The relative que then describes the gracia.
e: la incomparable riqueza de su gracia
Riqueza is singular despite the English idea of ‘riches.’ Incomparable intensifies the immeasurable quality of that grace.

g: Esto no ... sino que ...
The demonstrative esto summarizes the saving just described. No procede de ustedes is corrected by sino que es el regalo de Dios.
e: por gracia ustedes han sido salvados
The line repeats the declaration from verse 5, now adding mediante la fe to distinguish the basis, grace, from the means, faith.

g: Negative source + para que clause
‘No por obras’ denies works as the basis; ‘para que nadie se jacte’ uses subjunctive after para que to state the intended result.
e: para que nadie se jacte
Jactarse is reflexive and means ‘to boast.’ Nadie is a negative pronoun, so no additional no appears inside this subordinate clause.

g: Participial phrase modifying nosotros
‘Creados en Cristo Jesús’ agrees with the implied plural nosotros in somos hechura and states how that workmanship came about.
e: las pongamos en práctica
Poner algo en práctica means ‘to put something into practice.’ Las refers back to the feminine plural buenas obras.

g: Imperative followed by a parenthetical contrast
‘Recuerden’ is an ustedes command. The em-dash section contrasts two quoted group labels before the sentence resumes in the next verse.
e: por mano humana
This idiom means ‘by human hands.’ Por introduces the agent who performs the physical circumcision mentioned in the parenthesis.

g: Parallel predicate adjectives
‘Separados ..., excluidos ..., ajenos ..., sin esperanza y sin Dios’ stacks coordinated descriptions governed by estaban from this verse.
e: sin esperanza y sin Dios en el mundo
Repeated sin creates a forceful double absence: ‘without hope and without God in the world.’ Neither noun takes an article here.

g: A ustedes ... los: object doubling
‘A ustedes ... Dios los ha acercado’ states the object with a prepositional phrase and repeats it with direct-object pronoun los for clarity and emphasis.
e: mediante la sangre de Cristo
Mediante means ‘through’ or ‘by means of.’ The phrase identifies the means by which those formerly far away were brought near.

g: Gerund of accompanying means
‘Ha hecho uno solo, derribando ... el muro’ uses derribando to explain how the unifying action is carried out.
e: de los dos pueblos ha hecho uno solo
Hacer de dos uno is the pattern ‘to make one out of two.’ Uno solo stresses a single united people.

g: Purpose and means in one sentence
‘Para crear’ gives the purpose of anuló, while ‘al hacer la paz’ uses al + infinitive to express the action through which it occurs.
e: una nueva humanidad
Humanidad is a collective feminine noun. Here it renders the idea of a new united humanity formed from the two peoples.

g: Para + two coordinated infinitival purposes
‘Para reconciliar ...’ continues the purpose structure, and the later preterite ‘dio muerte’ states the result achieved through the cross.
e: a ambos en un solo cuerpo
Ambos means ‘both’ and functions as the personal object of reconciliar, so it takes personal a; en un solo cuerpo states their unity.

g: Parallel personal objects
‘Paz a ustedes que estaban lejos y paz a los que estaban cerca’ repeats paz and balances two recipient groups with matching relative clauses.
e: paz a ustedes que estaban lejos
The verse balances this phrase with paz a los que estaban cerca; the spatial opposites distinguish two recipient groups of the same proclaimed peace.

g: Access a + destination
Tener acceso a means ‘to have access to.’ A + el Padre contracts to al Padre, while por phrases name the mediation.
e: al Padre por un mismo Espíritu
The destination is al Padre and the means is por un mismo Espíritu. Mismo stresses that both groups share the one Spirit.

g: Ya no ... sino ...
‘Ya no son ... sino ...’ replaces a former identity with a new one: ‘you are no longer ... but rather ...’ Two positive nouns follow sino.
e: miembros de la familia de Dios
Miembro de means ‘member of.’ Familia shifts the image from civic belonging in conciudadanos to household belonging.

g: Two participial modifiers
‘Edificados sobre ...’ describes ustedes from verse 19, while ‘siendo Cristo ...’ supplies an accompanying clause naming the cornerstone.
e: la piedra angular
Piedra angular is the architectural ‘cornerstone,’ the stone used here to express Christ's defining place in the building image.

g: Ir + gerund for gradual development
‘Se va levantando’ combines ir with a gerund to show an unfolding process: the building ‘keeps rising’ toward becoming a temple.
e: todo el edificio
Todo before the article means ‘the whole building,’ not ‘every building.’ The singular image presents the joined structure as one unit.

g: Present passive + para ser
‘Son edificados juntamente para ser morada’ uses a present passive for the ongoing building and para ser for its intended function.
e: morada de Dios por su Espíritu
Morada is a formal word for a dwelling place. Por su Espíritu identifies the means or agency of God's dwelling in this communal image.
